newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh bank seeks probe of accounts.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh bank seeks probe of accounts.

text.p: Bangladesh Bank, the country's central bank, has ordered a probe of accounts held by Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria's daughter-in- law, Rina Sultana, after newspaper reports about a recent scam in the capital market, a bank official said on Thursday.
"We have been instructed by the Prime Minister's office to conduct the probe," the official told Reuters.
The central bank had issued a notice to all Bangladeshi commercial banks to conduct inquiries and report back, he said.
"This is not intended to malign anyone but to find out if the press reports contained any truth," said the official who declined to be identified.
A senior management official with a local bank confirmed his institution had received notice of the inquiry from the central bank.
The notice, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Thursday, said the commercial banks had to complete their probes within three days after the current Eid al-Adha festival.
"The time schedule is very tight. We may need an extension," one banker said.

Bangladeshi newspapers have reported that the probe was connected with Rina Sultana's share business and called on the . the finance minister to take the initiative and provide a clear picture of the situation.

Rina Sultana issued a strong protest, telling the Banglabazar Patrika newspaper she was "not involved in any unfair or illegal deals although she was in the share business". Every Bangladeshi citizen had a right to do share business, she told other reporters.
Kibria has not reacted to the press reports.

Last month an inquiry committee appointed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), watchdog of the country's capital market, said 36 top dealers and owners of companies listed with the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) had been involved in "fraudulent activities," causing losses to investors.

It said the accused, including DSE chairman Imtiyaz Husain, had manipulated share prices, sending the DSE index to soar above 3,600 points around the end of 1996 and then pushing it down to the level of 1,100 points.
Imtiyaz Husain has described the report as "baseless and motivated".

Following the inquiry report, a Dhaka court asked police to arrest the accused but they all obtained interim bail from the High Court. All the accused have been banned by the government from making foreign trips.
